windows:
  - window_name: should be /var/
    panes:
      - shell_command:
          - echo "\033c
          - it trickles down from session-level"
      - echo hello
  - window_name: should be /var/log
    start_directory: log
    panes:
      - shell_command:
          - echo '\033c
          - window start_directory concatenates to session start_directory
          - if it is not absolute'
      - echo hello
  - window_name: should be ~
    start_directory: "~"
    panes:
      - shell_command:
          - 'echo \\033c ~ has precedence. note: remember to quote ~ in YAML'
      - echo hello
  - window_name: should be /bin
    start_directory: /bin
    panes:
      - echo '\033c absolute paths also have precedence.'
      - echo hello
  - window_name: should be workspace file's dir

    start_directory: ./
    panes:
      - shell_command:
          - echo '\033c
          - ./ is relative to workspace file location
          - ../ will be parent of workspace file
          - ./test will be \"test\" dir inside dir of workspace file'
      - shell_command:
          - echo '\033c
          - This way you can load up workspaces from projects and maintain
          - relative paths.'

examples.note: `${PROJECT_ROOT}` and `${OPTION_TAG}` are variables the loader expands.
examples.yaml:
session_name: corpus
start_directory: ${PROJECT_ROOT}
options:
  default-command: exec /bin/sh
  '@corpus-session': yaml-original
environment:
  CORPUS_SESSION: yaml-root
  CORPUS_LAYER: session
shell_command_before:
  - cmd: echo session >> order.txt
windows:
  - window_name: yaml-editor
    start_directory: window
    layout: even-horizontal
    focus: true
    options:
      '@corpus-window': '${OPTION_TAG}'
    environment:
      CORPUS_WINDOW: yaml-window
      CORPUS_LAYER: window
    shell_command_before:
      - cmd: echo window >> order.txt
    panes:
      - shell_command:
          - cmd: echo command >> order.txt
          - 'echo "$CORPUS_SESSION|$CORPUS_WINDOW|$CORPUS_PANE|$CORPUS_LAYER" > environment.txt'
          - tmux wait-for -S corpus-yaml-first
      - start_directory: pane
        focus: true
        options:
          '@corpus-pane': yaml
        environment:
          CORPUS_PANE: yaml-pane
          CORPUS_LAYER: pane
        shell_command_before:
          - cmd: echo pane >> order.txt
        shell_command:
          - echo command >> order.txt
          - 'echo "$CORPUS_SESSION|$CORPUS_WINDOW|$CORPUS_PANE|$CORPUS_LAYER" > environment.txt'
          - tmux wait-for -S corpus-yaml-second
